what_its_for: Clascoterone is a prescription cream used to treat acne on the face and body in adults and teenagers 12 years of age and older. It works by blocking the effects of hormones (called androgens) in the skin that can cause acne breakouts.
how_to_take: Wash and gently dry the skin area where you plan to apply the cream before each use. Apply a thin, even layer of clascoterone 1% cream to the affected areas of your skin twice a day, in the morning and in the evening. Use only a small pea-sized amount for each area. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water right after applying the cream. Do not get the cream in your eyes, mouth, or nose. If it gets in these areas, rinse well with water right away. Do not cover the treated skin with tight bandages or wrappings unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: Apply a thin layer of clascoterone 1% cream to the affected skin areas two times every day — once in the morning and once in the evening. Your doctor may adjust this based on how your skin responds. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and do not use more or less than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not apply extra cream to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store clascoterone cream at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze the cream. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not store it in the bathroom, as moisture and heat can damage the cream. Dispose of unused or expired medication properly — ask your pharmacist how to safely throw it away.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting clascoterone cream in your eyes, mouth, nose, or on broken or irritated skin. Avoid applying other skincare products, cosmetics, or medicated creams to the same area at the same time unless your doctor says it is okay. Avoid using harsh soaps, abrasive scrubs, or skin products that can dry out or irritate your skin, such as those containing alcohol, spices, or astringents. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and tanning beds on treated skin — use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: severe skin irritation, redness, burning, or peeling where the cream was applied; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; unusual changes in your menstrual period; signs of adrenal gland problems such as unusual tiredness, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, weakness, or low blood pressure. Also contact your doctor if your acne is not improving after 4 to 8 weeks of use.
when_it_works: Clascoterone cream may start to reduce acne within 4 to 8 weeks of regular use, but it may take up to 12 weeks or longer to see the full benefit. Keep using it as directed even if you do not see immediate results. Do not stop using the cream without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Children under 12 years old: Safety and effectiveness have not been established in children younger than 12, so this medication should not be used in that age group. Teenagers 12 and older: This medication is approved and can be used safely under a doctor's supervision. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of clascoterone during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known. Older adults: No specific dosage adjustments are needed, but always follow your doctor's guidance. People with kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor about any kidney or liver conditions before using this medication.
